Title: Staff Software Engineer
Description: Elena brings nine years of full-stack experience, most recently as a staff engineer at a freight logistics startup where she led the React and TypeScript rebuild of the core dispatch platform used by two hundred carriers daily. She architected the accompanying Node.js microservices layer, deployed on AWS ECS with autoscaling and CI/CD pipelines she built from scratch. Elena mentors four engineers, runs the frontend guild's design reviews, and has deep firsthand knowledge of logistics challenges like real-time route optimization.

Title: Senior Frontend Engineer
Description: Marcus has spent six years as a frontend specialist, building complex React and TypeScript applications for two mid-size SaaS companies, including a design system used across a dozen product teams. His component architecture and state management skills are excellent, and he writes thorough unit tests. However, his backend experience is thin, mostly consuming REST APIs rather than building them, and he has never touched Node.js in production. His AWS exposure is limited to S3 and CloudFront, with no compute experience.

Title: Full-Stack Developer
Description: Aisha has four years of professional experience as a full-stack developer at a fintech startup, building customer-facing features end-to-end in React and Node.js/Express. Her code is clean, well-tested, and she's comfortable across the stack, including schema design in PostgreSQL. She falls just under the five-year bar the role targets, and her production AWS experience is limited; most of her cloud work with Lambda and DynamoDB comes from personal side projects rather than paid work.

Title: Senior Software Engineer
Description: Derek has eight years of backend experience building high-throughput services in Java and Spring Boot for a logistics and supply-chain company, with strong systems design chops around queuing, caching, and database sharding. He moved onto a React frontend eighteen months ago after his team absorbed a UI, and has since shipped several features, but his TypeScript is thin; he leans on the any type often, and hasn't worked with modern React patterns like server components or advanced hooks.

Title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer
Description: Ingrid has six years of full-stack experience at a digital agency, shipping React and Node.js applications across roughly fifteen client engagements ranging from e-commerce to internal tooling. She's comfortable picking up new codebases quickly and has broad exposure to AWS, Azure, and GCP deployments. Her resume shows real breadth, but most projects lasted only two to four months before handoff, making it hard to gauge depth of ownership or how her code held up in production over time.

Title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer
Description: Tyler's resume lists an unusually broad stack: React, Vue, Angular, Node.js, Go, Rust, Kubernetes, and 'AI/LLM engineering,' positioned as expert-level across all of them. His actual work history, however, shows three years at a small agency building WordPress themes and plugins for local business clients; no listed employer involved any of the claimed technologies. The skills section reads like a scan of current job postings, and there's no portfolio or shipped project corroborating any of the advanced claims made.

Title: Lead Engineer
Description: Chloe's headline claims she 'led a 20-person engineering org and drove a $40M platform migration' as a Lead Engineer. Her actual employment history tells a different story: two years as a junior QA analyst doing manual test execution at a mid-size retailer, followed by one year as a teaching assistant at a coding bootcamp grading beginner assignments. There is no engineering leadership role, no team of that size, and no platform of that scale anywhere in her history.

Title: Senior Developer
Description: Viktor's skills section lists over thirty technologies, including TypeScript, React, Node.js, AWS, Kubernetes, and GraphQL, suggesting deep full-stack and cloud breadth. But every bullet under his three prior roles reads identically generic: 'worked on features,' 'fixed bugs,' 'collaborated with the team,' 'improved performance.' No employer, product, or project is ever named anywhere in his history, no metrics are given. Without one concrete example of what he actually built, the long skills list can't be verified.

Title: Registered Nurse
Description: Rosa has ten years of experience as a Registered Nurse in ICU settings, with deep clinical expertise in critical care, patient triage, and cross-functional coordination with physicians and specialists. She recently completed a six-week introductory coding bootcamp covering basic HTML, CSS, and JavaScript fundamentals, and her application note says she's 'open to anything in tech' as she explores a career change. She has no professional software experience, no completed projects beyond bootcamp exercises, and no exposure to React or Node.js.

Title: Account Executive
Description: Ben has seven years of experience as an Account Executive in B2B SaaS sales, consistently exceeding quota and managing a pipeline of enterprise logistics accounts. He has strong relationship-building skills and a track record of closing complex, multi-stakeholder deals across long sales cycles. His application note describes him as 'great with people' and someone who 'learns fast,' and expresses interest in a technical role. He has no engineering background and no coding experience listed on his resume.

Title: Software Engineer II
Description: Grace has three years of experience as a Software Engineer II, building React features for an internal admin dashboard and occasionally writing small Node.js endpoints to support them. Her code reviews are clean and she communicates well with product stakeholders, but she hasn't owned a service end-to-end or worked directly with cloud infrastructure; deployments are handled by a separate platform team, so she has no hands-on AWS experience. She's dependable, but her level sits below the five-plus years targeted.

Title: Backend Engineer
Description: Liam has five years of backend engineering experience building Django applications and REST APIs for an internal logistics data platform, with particularly strong SQL skills honed through complex reporting queries and schema optimization work. His JavaScript exposure is minimal, a handful of small jQuery scripts and a few React tweaks made under supervision, and he's never built a frontend application independently. He's a capable backend engineer, but the role's React and TypeScript needs sit outside his skill set.

Title: Mobile Engineer
Description: Yuki has six years of experience as a mobile engineer, building and shipping React Native applications for a consumer logistics tracking app used by hundreds of thousands of riders. Her React fundamentals are strong and transfer reasonably well toward web development, including hooks, state management, and component composition. However, all of her experience is client-side; she has never built or maintained a Node.js backend service, and her AWS exposure is limited to reading logs from other teams' services.

Title: DevOps Engineer
Description: Fatima has five years of experience as a DevOps engineer, with deep expertise in AWS infrastructure, Terraform, CI/CD pipeline design, and Kubernetes cluster management for a mid-size logistics software company. She's the go-to person for incident response and infrastructure cost optimization on her team. Her application-code experience is comparatively light, however; she's written small automation scripts in Python and some infrastructure-adjacent Node.js tooling, but never built a customer-facing feature in React or owned a service end-to-end.

Title: Full-Stack Engineer
Description: Carlos has five years of full-stack engineering experience building e-commerce and logistics applications with PHP, Laravel, and Vue.js for a regional retailer. He's comfortable across the stack, from database schema design to frontend component work, and has shipped several customer-facing features independently and on schedule. His React experience, however, comes only from online tutorials and small personal projects; he has never used it professionally, and his TypeScript exposure is essentially nonexistent, having worked mostly in vanilla JavaScript and PHP.

Title: Senior QA Engineer
Description: Hannah has eight years of experience as a senior QA engineer, building and maintaining large TypeScript test automation suites with Playwright for a logistics platform, including custom tooling that cut regression cycle time significantly. She reads and writes TypeScript fluently and understands the application's architecture from the testing side. She's actively looking to transition into feature development and has started contributing small bug fixes, but has no professional experience owning feature work or React component design.

Title: Solutions Architect
Description: Omar has twelve years of experience in enterprise software, most recently as a Solutions Architect designing integration patterns between logistics, ERP, and CRM systems for large enterprise clients. He has deep knowledge of system design, API contracts, and cross-team technical strategy, and is a strong communicator with both engineering and business stakeholders. For the past four years, his role has been largely hands-off from code, reviewing designs rather than shipping features, so his hands-on React and Node.js skills are dated.
